summary:
AIR DETECTIVE – INDIA is an interactive web application developed to explore air pollution across 15 major Indian cities. It features an interactive map of India with state boundaries, colour-coded pollution levels, and city markers. Users can view current air-quality estimates, explore pollutants such as PM2.5, PM10, NO₂, SO₂, O₃ and CO, and compare pollution levels between cities through interactive charts.

The project addresses the challenge of making complex Earth-system data easier to understand and explore. By presenting atmospheric data through maps and visualisations, it helps users identify differences in estimated air pollution across locations.

This project is important because air pollution affects environmental quality and human well-being. AIR DETECTIVE – INDIA encourages environmental awareness and makes air-quality information more accessible to the public.

The application uses the Open-Meteo Air Quality API, which provides CAMS-based atmospheric model estimates.

details:
AIR DETECTIVE – INDIA

1. What does the project do, and how does it work?

AIR DETECTIVE – INDIA is an interactive web application that helps users explore air pollution across 15 major Indian cities. When users open the website, an interactive map of India loads automatically, displaying state boundaries, city markers, and colour-coded pollution levels. Users can explore current air-quality estimates, view different pollutants such as PM2.5, PM10, NO₂, SO₂, O₃ and CO, and compare pollution levels between cities using interactive charts.

2. What are its benefits?

The project makes air-quality information easier to understand through maps, colours, and visualisations. Instead of reading complicated datasets, users can explore pollution information in a simple and interactive way. It also helps users understand how estimated pollution levels differ between cities.

3. What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to increase awareness about air pollution and encourage people to pay more attention to environmental conditions. We hope the project makes environmental information more accessible and inspires people to think about protecting the planet.

4. What tools, coding languages, and software were used?

The project was developed using:

  • Python: Main programming language.
  • Streamlit: To build the interactive web application.
  • Pandas: To organise and process data.
  • Plotly: To create interactive charts.
  • Folium: To create the interactive map.
  • Streamlit-Folium: To display the map inside the application.
  • Requests: To retrieve data from APIs.
  • Open-Meteo Air Quality API: Provides CAMS-based atmospheric air-quality estimates.
  • geoBoundaries: Used for geographical state boundaries.
  • OpenStreetMap: Used for map tiles.
  • GitHub and Streamlit Community Cloud: Used for code hosting and website deployment.

No specialised hardware was required. Development was carried out using a computer and an internet connection.

5. How is the project creative?

The creative aspect of AIR DETECTIVE – INDIA is the way it combines geographical maps, colour-coded pollution information, and interactive charts in one website. Users can explore different cities and compare multiple pollutants without needing technical knowledge. The map loads automatically when the website opens, making the experience simple and convenient.

6. What factors did the team consider?

We considered simplicity, accessibility, data availability, performance, and ease of use. We wanted the website to load smoothly without unnecessary data processing. Therefore, we focused on current air-quality readings rather than large hourly datasets. We also considered the importance of presenting data clearly and being transparent about its source and limitations.

Our vision: To make environmental data easier to explore, understand, and use to encourage a cleaner and healthier planet.
